709195.t: From Phoenician (compare Hebrew נֵרְדְּ (nērd), Aramaic נִרְדָּא (nirdā), Akkadian 𒆠𒆗 (HIRIM /⁠lardu⁠/), Arabic رَنْد (rand), Old South Arabian 𐩧𐩬𐩵 (rnd)), possibly from Sanskrit नलद (nálada, “Indian narde”) (although a Semitic-to-Indian loan has also been…

709191.t: From Proto-Hellenic *nahwós, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *nes- (“to join with, to conceal oneself”) and related to ναίω (naíō, “to dwell”), νέομαι (néomai, “to go or come back”).

709110.t: Of unclear origin. Traditionally compared with Sanskrit मूर (mūrá, “dull, stupid, foolish”), from Proto-Indo-European *mowHrós, *muHrós (“dull, stupid”), with ablaut *ō(u) : *ū.

709102.t: Uncertain. The term has traditionally been compared to ἀμύμων (ămū́mōn, “blameless”), though Beekes rejects this proposal, arguing that the ablaut variation of ω ~ υ (ō ~ u) is impossible.

709177.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *nes- (“to join with, to conceal oneself”), but Beekes considers this uncertain. See νέομαι (néomai, “to go or come back”).

709162.t: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew נָזִיר (nāzîr, “Nazarite”), perhaps from נִזַּר (nizzar, “separate; consecrate oneself”).

709193.t: According to Beekes, probably of Pre-Greek origin.
